To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the microstructure of the Nb–Ti micro-alloyed X90 steel is primarily composed of the non-equiaxed grains with M/A constituent dispersed at the grain boundaries.

the microstructure evolution is the key factor for the tensile properties of Nb–Ti micro-alloyed X90 steel, and the finish rolling temperature plays an important role on the evolution of microstructure.

the yield strength and YR increase with decreasing finish rolling temperature due to the increase in grain refinement strengthening contribution, dislocation strengthening contribution and decrease in precipitation strengthening contribution.

the microstructure evolution and tensile properties for Nb–Ti micro alloyed X90 pipeline steels with different finish rolling temperature, which provides an important reference for the development of X90 pipeline steel.
the effect of finish rolling temperature on the microstructure and mechanical properties of an Nb-Ti microalloyed pipeline steel.
the relationship between microstructure evolution and mechanical properties of the Nb–Ti micro alloyed X90 pipeline steels as a function of the finish rolling temperature.

the finish rolling temperature has a significant influence on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the Nb–Ti micro-alloyed X90 steel.
the tensile properties of the microalloyed steel are strongly dependent on microstructural characteristics, and the microstructural features can be controlled by finish rolling temperature.

the tensile properties can be improved by decreasing the finish rolling temperatures, although the strain hardening ability decreases, due to the grain refinement strengthening and dislocation strengthening contributions.
